statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-124742 (Red Hat bug https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2571620): the volume_id FAT prober used by blkid, findfs and mount LABEL=/UUID= skipped its geometry checks when the boot sector carried a magic string such as "FAT16   ", so a sectors_per_cluster value of 0 was later used as a divisor and a crafted filesystem image crashed the prober. The Debian tracker lists busybox as unfixed in trixie with urgency unimportant: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-124742 . Upstream fixed it with commit https://github.com/vda-linux/busybox_mirror/commit/b7c89c493a889e749d98cd9b7fd55be124639215 , which moves the cluster size check in util-linux/volume_id/fat.c ahead of the magic-string checks. DHI backports that commit, and the fixed version is the first build that carries it. We disassembled volume_id_probe_vfat in /usr/bin/busybox from the busybox and busybox-static packages of all five published builds of 1:1.37.0-6+deb13u0, on amd64 and arm64, using the symbol tables in the -dbgsym packages: from the fixed build on, the zero and power-of-two test of sectors_per_cluster runs right after the superblock is read, before the magic-string comparisons; the three earlier builds have identical code with the test after them.
